title: Proposed congressional approval of major rules and the major-questions connection
shortTitle: Proposed congressional approval of major rules and the major-questions connection
summary: The notes distinguish a proposed legislative approval requirement from a judicial demand for clear authorization over major questions.
notes:
The text describes the REINS Act proposals in the Congresses it discusses as requiring a joint resolution satisfying bicameralism and presentment before certain major agency rules become effective, subject to stated exceptions. It reports that those proposals had not been enacted in that historical account. The mechanism would change delegated authority through legislation.

The adjacent note introduces the major-questions doctrine as requiring clear statutory authority for decisions of great economic or political significance and reports disagreement over its constitutional or interpretive foundation. Gorsuch links it to nondelegation, while Barrett rejects that particular grounding. Later assigned readings supply the developed doctrine; this introductory note is not a current legislative-status check or a complete major-questions case account.
